tasks.task: Design a course outline back from one result

items.when: When you know what the learner must be able to do and need modules, goals and evidence
Before the outline, to break the skill into steps a beginner can learn with the usual mistakes
When the know-how sits in one expert's head and must be drawn out from real cases
When the course is for staff, to get a second outline built from the real work problem
When the outline covers every topic and never makes learners practise the hard part

tasks.task: Turn an SOP, policy or expert notes into teachable content

items.when: When a client hands over source material and needs a self-paced module through to launch
When the procedure is not written down yet and must be captured and gap-checked first
When one part is known to confuse people and you need the usual mistakes and examples
When the source is old or second-hand, to check its facts before they are taught

tasks.task: Write a screen-by-screen e-learning storyboard

items.when: When the outline is agreed and a developer needs numbered screens to build from
Before fixing the screens, to see several ways to present the content and let learners respond
When a screen must teach a skill step by step with help that fades
When a concept needs a diagram or table placed where it helps the explanation
When the storyboard is drafted, to find screens that overload the learner
Before it goes to the developer, to cut excess and fix barriers

tasks.task: Write lesson pages or scripts with exercises

items.when: When you have the topic and learners and need a lesson, examples, practice and a quiz
When the lesson opens with the explanation, to try a version where learners attempt first
When an idea needs the smallest example that still shows how it works
When the lesson needs exercises that rise in difficulty
When the page is drafted, to find where it asks too much at once

tasks.task: Write a branching scenario with feedback for every choice

items.when: When learners must practise a hard conversation or decision with tempting wrong choices
When the scenario is a hard talk and you need what a skilled person would really say
When each wrong choice should reveal one known mistake, not a silly option
When the decision points and paths need a map the builder can paste into docs
When the best path reads like a policy and not like how people talk under pressure

tasks.task: Write knowledge checks that test doing the job

items.when: When a module needs questions that test the task, not a remembered definition
When questions should push past recall to why and how
When a short quiz should end the course and bring back the key points
When the questions are drafted, to check they test the goals and not tricks or reading speed

tasks.task: Set certification rules and write the exam

items.when: When the exam needs job-based questions for each goal in the course
When passing should mean doing a real task, with a scoring guide
When a practical task needs clear wording for each level of work
Before the exam counts, to check every question maps to something taught

tasks.task: Write a training or how-to video script

items.when: When one task needs a two-column script with narration beside what is on screen
When the presenter must show their thinking aloud, not only the clicks
When you have screenshots and want a short walkthrough video or GIF made from them
When an approved lesson needs a checked spoken script and a text version to follow
When nobody will go on camera and the script needs an AI presenter
When a screen recording needs trimming and cleaning by editing its transcript

tasks.task: Make captions, narration and other-language versions

items.when: When the script is final and captions must be ready to upload
When a video is already recorded and needs a timed transcript and subtitle file
When the narration needs spoken audio without booking a voice artist
When the same video must go out in other languages with the voice kept
When captions need adding and checking in a browser with no install

tasks.task: Write an email or chat micro-course

items.when: When one practical skill should be taught in short lessons by email, text or Slack
Before writing lessons, to compare three plans for how the series could unfold
When the order of lessons is unclear and each must build on the last
When a lesson email is drafted, to get cuts, subject fixes and a score
When each lesson tells and none asks the learner to recall or try anything

tasks.task: Write the welcome, invite and launch emails for a course

items.when: When new sign-ups need a welcome series that teaches before it asks
When the course opens on a date and needs a launch plan through to the close
When the price is not set and the launch emails depend on it
Before drafting, to compare three different shapes for the series
Before each email is scheduled, to get cuts and a verdict
Before the launch emails are written, to confirm the sign-up link, price and start date work today

tasks.task: Write an honest course sales page and price note

items.when: Before any sales copy, to state the one result the course can honestly promise
When the course needs a name, a guarantee and payment terms before the page is written
When you have learner reviews, to get a buyer brief and two openings to compare
When the offer is set and the page needs hero, value points, proof and a call to act
When the page is drafted, to find the weakest parts and fix them
Before publishing, to check every promised outcome is true and has context
Before writing the page, to confirm enrolment is open, the price is as stated and the dates are still ahead

tasks.task: Review a module, page or video for accessibility

items.when: Before a module goes live, or when an existing course gets a complaint
When the course is a web page and needs ranked problems against the standard
When the module was built from slides and needs titles, reading order and alt text fixed
When the barrier may be in the lesson design itself, not the page code
When the course library changes often and needs a recheck each quarter

tasks.task: Choose and test the LMS package

items.when: When a module is ready and nobody knows which output to pick, or it fails in one LMS
When the module reaches the publish step and the launch checks must run in order

tasks.task: Plan a customer academy from support tickets

items.when: When a company wants customers to learn the product without opening tickets
When the same support questions keep coming and should become short courses by role
When you have a ticket export and need themes ranked by how often they come up
When the academy must fit phased onboarding steps for new customers
When a topic is better as a searchable help article than a lesson
When the product has changed, to check each tutorial still matches the screens

tasks.task: Keep the academy current and report ticket deflection

items.when: When the academy is live and the monthly upkeep and report are due
Each month, to find lessons that are stale or hard to follow
When tickets must be sorted by topic to compare volume before and after a course
When the deflection numbers need a report you can rerun each month

tasks.task: Plan staff, onboarding or compliance training

items.when: When a skills gap must become ranked needs, objectives and a training plan
When training should start from one real work problem with measurable goals
When the plan is agreed and each course needs an outline built from its result
After compliance training, to see whether staff follow the policy and what blocks them

tasks.task: Make job aids, handouts and explainer visuals

items.when: When a session needs a one-page handout people can use at their desk
When content suits a picture, to see it in a layout and style picked to fit
When one concept needs a simple diagram or table
When the handout is drafted, to find where it crams in too much

tasks.task: Check a lesson or module before it goes live

items.when: When a lesson is drafted and needs a lighter version and barriers fixed
When you know the learners and want the barriers this group will hit
When a task is dull or stressful and people are likely to quit there
When learners get stuck on how the module works, not on the content

tasks.task: Read course results and decide what to fix

items.when: When you have quiz results or LMS numbers and need what they mean and what to change
After the course, to compare real work with the skills taught
When fixes should be found and tracked lesson by lesson each month

always.when: Before learners see it, to check the facts in scripts, screens and answers
Before any screen, page or handout is handed over, to find where it asks too much

helpers.when: When a training video must be filmed, edited and delivered, not only scripted
When the course sales page needs full selling copy and testing
When launch and welcome emails need lists, timing and sending set up
When the module must pass a formal accessibility standard
When the academy needs help articles and product docs beside the lessons
When the course is part of a wider staff skills plan with managers involved

gaps: No library item writes an e-learning storyboard; storyboard searches returned ad and film items
No library item writes a branching scenario, offers different scenario structures to compare, or tests a map for dead ends
No library item helps choose or test SCORM, xAPI or cmi5 output, or gives an LMS upload test list
No library item writes a screen recording or procedure demo script; video script items are for ads
No library item writes scenario-based questions for job tasks; quiz items are built for classroom recall
No library item writes an email, text or chat course that teaches; email sequence items are built to sell
No library item designs an adult or online course outline back from one result; unit planners assume school standards
No library item plans a customer academy by user role or measures ticket deflection
No library item sets certification rules such as pass mark, retakes and expiry
No library item writes a learner feedback survey or evaluates a course at more than quiz level
No library item gives build notes for Rise, Storyline or course platforms such as Teachable or Kajabi
No library item finds where learners drop out of a course and why
